summary: Orchard & Co. and Redwood ran a detailed alignment session focused on uptime targets, capacity sizing, and unit economics for a proposed 30-day pilot. Primary concerns were p95 latency at peak, data residency/VPC, and finance sign-off. Redwood AE+SE committed to latency benchmarks, pricing, and security artifacts. Next step: pilot kickoff scheduling and pilot SOW.
topics: Current production traffic shape + p95 targets
Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
Pilot scope, pricing, and finance approval timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through uptime, capacity and the cost alignment for the pilot. Quick intro, Maya from Redwood, Ben our SE.
[00:09] Lena: Hey, Lena here, Head of ML at Orchard & Co. Derrick on platform, Sara from finance.
[00:15] Ben: Morning — I'll drive the benchmarks later in this call. We have some sample throughput numbers but want to validate your shape.
[00:22] Derrick: Right, for context our peak is ~1,200 qps for short prompts and about 150 qps for longer conversations during launches, also bursty around midday.
[00:33] Sara: From finance side, we need a clear cost per 1M tokens and committed capacity pricing to get approval.
[00:40] Maya: Totally, we can do committed pricing. First question — what are your p95 latency targets?
[00:45] Lena: For critical flows we really need p95 <= 220 ms for 32-token generations. For multi-turn chat where we have history, p95 can be up to 800 ms, but we want consistency.
[00:57] Ben: That's reasonable. The main lever is dedicated capacity with lower variance vs hosted. There's also quantization and batching knobs.
[01:05] Speaker 1: (inaudible) batching maybe affects tail latencies a bit.
[01:10] Derrick: We prefer to avoid variability; bursts shouldn't increase p95 past 350. Also, data can't leave EU region for some customers — we need residency.
[01:18] Maya: Got it, we'll map regions. For residency we can do Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated in EU region. On the dedicated side we provide reserved GPU pools which lowers latency variance.
[01:29] Ben: Quick note on runtime: our engine supports continuous batching and prefix/KV cache. In some recordings the transcript shows K V cash rather than KV cache — sorry, auto-transcription fun.
[01:40] Lena: (laughs) yes the transcription did that. But can you explain how KV caching helps with multi-turn chat?
[01:45] Ben: KV caching avoids recomputing past attention keys and values so the effective cost and latency for subsequent turns drop dramatically. If your median turn length is short, the cache gives strong savings.
[01:55] Sara: Are there extra fees for caching or is it included?
[01:58] Maya: It's included in Dedicated; on hosted we recommend caching layers and we show the econ delta in the cost model. We'll include a sample cost-model.xlsx with and without caching.
[02:09] Lena: Security — we need SOC 2 type II evidence, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, SSO with SAML, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:18] Ben: We have SOC 2 attestation, KMS with HSM options for Redwood Private and dedicated key wrapping for hosted. SSO SAML is supported; RBAC is configurable. We can push audit logs (API calls, tensor traces are scrubbed) to your Splunk.
[02:31] Derrick: For VPC/networking: do you support private peering and do we need to open egress?
[02:36] Maya: Yes, we have VPC peering and VPN options. For Private deployments we can provide an air-gapped package if required, though that needs enterprise legal sign-off.
[02:46] Lena: Great. On cost tradeoffs, can you summarize hosted vs dedicated quickly?
[02:50] Ben: Hosted is low friction and you pay per-token. Dedicated is reserved GPUs: you get lower and more predictable p95 latency and often better unit costs at higher throughput. Tradeoff is commitment and some setup. Our optimize toolkit suggests batching/quantization profiles to hit cost targets.
[03:06] Sara: We're worried about unexpected token runaways spiking cost. Are there rate limit / quota guardrails?
[03:11] Maya: Yes, per-route quotas and token budgets. We can set alerts and automatic fallbacks to smaller models if thresholds hit.
[03:19] Speaker 2: question about model rollback policy — how fast can you fallback?
[03:23] Ben: Canary policies can be automated; fallback to a compatible, slightly cheaper variant is typically sub- minute once triggered. We'll show a config snippet.
[03:31] Lena: For pilot scope, we want 30 days across EU region, include 4 endpoints: search assist, checkout chat, post-purchase email drafts, and analytics embeddings. Can Redwood support embeddings at scale?
[03:44] Ben: Yes — embeddings are supported with batching and dedupe caching. We'll propose a throughput plan.
[03:51] Derrick: About benchmarks — we'd like both synthetic and replayed traffic from our logs to see real behavior.
[03:56] Maya: Absolutely, Ben will run both. We'll need a sanitized replay sample.
[04:02] Ben: I'll ask for a 30-min sample trace. We'll run 32-token and 512-token profiles plus multi-turn sequences. Expect a results doc and raw logs.
[04:13] Maya: On the pricing horizon — Sara, what's the earliest finance can sign off?
[04:17] Sara: If we have a clear pilot quote and the spend is under our one-time approver threshold, we can sign in the first week of July, otherwise it needs board review.
[04:25] Maya: Understood. We'll aim to keep pilot at a predictable committed bucket to avoid board-level approvals.
[04:31] Lena: One more thing — we have internal concerns about model regression and hallucination for checkout messages. Any eval tooling?
[04:39] Ben: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets and evals; we can add regression alerts tied to your test prompts. We'll also include eval harness examples.
[04:48] Derrick: For the pilot environment, how do you handle logs retention and PII scrubbing?
[04:53] Maya: Logs retention is configurable per account. We recommend early PII scrubbing; for Private deployments you can opt to keep logs in your S3 and disable retention on Redwood side.
[05:04] Speaker 1: small crosstalk about on prem options.
[05:09] Ben: Operationally, we'll instrument token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards in Redwood Console so your SREs can triage.
[05:18] Lena: Okay — do you have a suggested capacity to start the pilot?
[05:21] Ben: Based on the 1,200 qps peak short prompts plus bursts, I'd suggest a dedicated pool sized at 80% headroom with autoscale bursting to 150% for launch days. We'll provide concrete GPU counts and expected p95 numbers in the benchmark report.
[05:36] Sara: Can you also show the amortized cost per user and per-transaction in the cost model? That's key for our product folks.
[05:42] Maya: Yes, cost-model.xlsx will include per-call, per-user and per-month amortized lines.
[05:48] Derek: (misattributed name) Sorry, Derrick: what about SLOs? If you miss p95, is there credit or remediation?
[05:55] Maya: For Dedicated customers we have SLA remedies and runbooks; for pilots we offer committed uptime targets and remediation support. We'll include the SLA excerpt in the SOW.
[06:04] Lena: Alright, recap then?
[06:06] Maya: Recap: Redwood will 1) run benchmarks (Ben) with synthetic + replay, 2) send pilot SOW + committed pricing (Maya), 3) get your infra details and residency constraints (Derrick), 4) Sara to confirm finance window. Target dates in action items.
[06:22] Sara: Sounds good. Thank you.
[06:24] Maya: We'll follow up with the cost spreadsheet, pilot SOW and schedule the kickoff for early July.
[06:30] Lena: Thanks all.
[06:33] Ben: Thanks, bye.
notes: Benchmarks to include: p95 numbers for 32/512 tokens, multi-turn KV cache impact, throughput scaling table
